Task_Type.reason: Confirmed. The study's task is subphenotype discovery. GNN embeddings of longitudinal OneFlorida+ EHR encounters are clustered (time-series k-means with DTW) into four MCI-to-AD progression subphenotypes. The subphenotypes are then characterised (comorbidities, Kaplan-Meier survival after AD diagnosis) and predicted from pre-MCI information (AUROC 0.67-0.70). Every included patient converted: inclusion required 'a conversion time to the AD of more than six months' (p.5), and the cohort's mean MCI-to-AD time is 891 days (p.9). So there is no stable-MCI group and no pMCI-vs-sMCI or conversion prediction. The only other model output is the GNN's auxiliary next-encounter stage forecast ('preclinical, MCI, and AD', p.7). That is a three-class representation-learning objective used to shape the embeddings, and its metrics appear only in supplementary eTables 2-5. The template maps to T2 'ONLY if the task is explicitly progressive vs stable MCI or MCI-to-AD conversion', and subtype studies are T4.
